page: Amazon Web Services m5n.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by Intel Xeon 8259CL processors running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance exposes all 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated execution threads directly without hypervisor overhead. System resources include 384.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per thread. Network connectivity provides a 100 Gbps baseline interface optimized for data-intensive networking, while local storage is absent, requiring external Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel throughput and system interconnect speeds. In multi-threaded evaluation, the platform scored 82,015.21 in stress-ng and 57,124.09 in the PassMark CPU test suite, placing it in the top quartile of evaluated instances. Synthetic memory throughput tests measured 219.15 GB/sec for uncached read blocks and 95.5 GB/sec for large block writes. These throughput capabilities translate into strong application-tier performance, demonstrated by 77.84 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 48.53 GB/sec in static web throughput, and elevated scores in Clang compilation and ray tracing. Conversely, single-core metrics fall within average median ranges, scoring 1,334.0 on Geekbench single-core and 1,458.19 on stress-ng single-core.

The absence of accelerators limits autoregressive language model text generation, which scored in the bottom quartile across medium and small models. Additionally, workloads requiring low-latency scratch disks must account for the lack of bundled local NVMe storage. Overall cost efficiency is driven by the density of dedicated physical cores and 100 Gbps network capacity, making m5n.metal suited for network-heavy microservices, enterprise Clang compilation clusters, large Redis caching tiers, and distributed database nodes that leverage network-attached storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server featuring 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated threads on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz. Backed by 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz and a high-throughput 100 Gbps network interface, it bypasses hypervisor virtualization layers entirely. The server delivers top-tier parallel compute, scoring 82,015.21 on multi-core stress-ng benchmarks and achieving 77.84 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. It features hardware instructions including AVX-512 VNNI, but lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs. While single-thread execution and AI text generation perform at or below median levels, its high memory throughput and networking bandwidth deliver efficient compute density for network-bound container clusters, parallel software compilation, and large-scale in-memory key-value stores.
